caption: A plastic soda bottle is left too close to a campfire, and the near side shrivels and caves in.

sa.check: A plastic bottle stands near a campfire.
The side facing the fire shrivels.
The far side keeps its shape.
The bottle is smooth at the start.
The shrivelling comes first and the caving follows.

pc.expect: The plastic on the fire side goes soft, wrinkles and pulls inward, keeping its plastic look, while the rest stays a rigid bottle.
pc.fail: The bottle shatters into pieces; or the whole bottle runs into a puddle at once; or the fire side stays perfectly smooth while caving deeply; or the bottle stretches upward like taffy.

pc.expect: The caving only deepens on the fire side and the caved side does not pop back out.
pc.fail: The caved side pops back out to smooth while the bottle stays by the fire; or the caving deepens and eases in turn; or the far side caves while the fire side stays smooth; or the shrivelling appears before the bottle is near the fire.

pc.expect: The change is strongest on the side toward the fire and least on the far side.
pc.fail: The far side shrivels while the fire side stays smooth; or the bottle shrivels evenly all round while the fire is plainly on one side; or the bottle caves in at its base while its fire-facing wall stays smooth.

pc.expect: The bottle stays standing or topples downward as it softens, and its contents stay in it and lie level.
pc.fail: The bottle rises off the ground; or the bottle leans further and further over without falling; or the contents climb the bottle's wall and stay; or the bottle floats toward the fire.

pc.expect: One bottle; it keeps its cap and label and does not pass through the ground.
pc.fail: The bottle vanishes; or a second bottle appears; or the cap passes into the bottle; or the bottle sinks into the ground.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The bottle's label, the fire's stones and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The label's printing changes; or the stones rearrange; or the background changes between frames.

note: Smoke or discolouring from the melting plastic is chemistry and is not judged.
